name: compute_xor_checksum
description: Walks a block of 32-bit longwords, XORing each into an accumulator for a count taken from the size argument. It returns the accumulator masked to keep every other bit, so the checksum uses only the alternating-bit pattern.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:0788
name: fill_block_alternating_pattern
description: Fills a memory block with an alternating-bit longword pattern, writing eight longwords per pass backwards from the end of the block. The block length is chosen from a flag byte in the caller's structure, selecting one of two sizes.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:07BA
name: interleave_word_bits
description: Merges two bit-planes stored 128 longwords apart: it keeps the even-numbered bits of the second source and moves the even-numbered bits of the first source into the odd positions. The combined longword is written to the output, repeated for 128 longwords.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:07E2
name: repeat_mix_store_calls
description: Runs a loop of paired calls to other routines, with the iteration count derived from the first argument, then makes two more calls. It returns both incoming arguments unchanged.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:0810
name: update_flag_byte_after_mix
description: Calls the bitwise mix-store routine twice, then reads the byte at the address register. It sets the top bit when the low bit of the preceding byte is clear, unless bit six is already set, and clears the top bit when that low bit is set, then writes the byte back.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:081A
name: set_flag_byte_top_bit
description: Reads the byte at the address register and updates its top bit using the low bit of the preceding byte: it sets the top bit when that flag is clear, unless bit six is already set, and clears it when the flag is set. The result is written back.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:0864
name: start_disk_read_dma
description: Writes two control values to set up the disk controller, then the standard disk sync word, and stores the buffer address in the disk pointer register. It starts a read whose length is half the value passed in the data register, with the enable bit set.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:08A2
name: check_status_bit_configure_timer
description: Calls a routine, then reads bit one of a status byte at an offset from its returned address. If that bit is set it writes a pair of timer control values and returns zero; if not, it calls a routine again, writes the same pair in reverse order, and returns minus one.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:08DA
name: write_adkcon_conditional_bit
description: Writes a fixed control value to the ADKCON register, then, when a signed value in the caller's frame is negative, writes a byte built from a computed bit index to the same register.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:08EA
name: set_bit_in_global_flag
description: Takes a value from the caller's frame, offsets it by three and uses the low five bits as a bit position. It sets that bit in the data byte passed in and writes the result to the CIA port register.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:0908
name: reset_ciab_port_then_wait
description: Writes all ones to the CIA port register, calls a called routine once, then repeatedly calls it again and waits while the low bit of the port register stays set, until the call returns one. Returns zero.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:0920
name: update_table_entry
description: Reads a 16-bit entry from a global table at an index taken from the caller's frame; if the entry is negative it calls a called routine and returns that result when non-zero. Otherwise it calls a routine once per unit of difference between the new and stored values, stores the new value into the table entry, and returns zero.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:096E
name: wait_for_input_flag_clear
description: Polls the port register for bit four, calling a routine between polls for up to 86 iterations. When the bit clears it zeroes a table entry indexed by a frame value and returns zero; otherwise it returns a timeout value of thirty.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:09A2
name: arm_ciab_port_and_wait
description: Reads the port register through a called routine, clears bit one when a sign value from the caller is non-negative, and sets bit zero to start an operation. It then calls a routine repeatedly and waits while bit zero stays set, until that call returns one, and returns zero.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:09C6
name: store_helper_result_to_port

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:09D0
name: build_port_mask_byte
description: Builds a mask byte from the port register value, clearing a bit chosen by an index in the caller's frame, and also clears bit two when the table entry for that index has its low bit set. It returns the high word of the data register, the mask, and the low word of the second input.

key: Assassin (1992)(Team 17)[cr CSL](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$2C00 to $078000 (4608 bytes):0:0A00
name: wait_for_flag_and_result
description: Calls a routine and, while the low bit of the port register stays set, waits; it repeats until the call returns one, then returns zero.

name: configure_cia_timer_if_idle

name: copy_block_longs_backwards
description: Copies longwords backwards in eight-longword steps from a source area into a destination that is first aligned to an even address, then copies a fixed block of 56 longword pairs from a global area to the destination.

name: run_text_bitplane_state_machine
description: Runs a frame-synchronised state machine: one state copies glyph bytes from a null-terminated text into eight bitplane row pointers, another computes a quadratic offset per column and draws the resulting positions through a routine, and the remaining states count delays and advance pointers.

name: reload_audio_channel_pointers
description: Advances a frame counter; when it wraps, it calls a routine four times, waits through two timed delay loops, and reloads the four audio location registers from stored addresses. Otherwise it calls a routine and continues into a shared update that resets counters.

name: process_audio_channel_command
description: Decodes a 16-bit command for one audio channel and, depending on its nibble, applies a volume step, a period change or a playback position update. The result is written to that channel's hardware registers and returned.

name: run_audio_channel_sequencer
description: Steps one audio channel's note sequence: it reads four-byte entries, loads the channel's start address and length from a table, and executes a command switch that sets volume, slide or length values. It writes the resulting address and length to the channel registers.

name: decode_channel_command_entry
description: Decodes a 16-bit command stored in a channel structure and applies a volume, slide, period or playback update of the same kind as the audio command decoder. It stores the result in the structure's output field and returns it.

name: copy_struct_word_to_output
description: Copies a 16-bit field from the caller's structure at one offset into an output field at another offset, with no other work.

name: find_table_slot_for_value
description: Searches a 37-entry word table, selected by a byte in the structure, for the first entry not below the structure's current value, and stores that entry as the target. If a flag bit is set and the search index is not zero it steps back one entry, and it sets a direction flag when the target is below the current value.

name: step_value_toward_target
description: Moves a stored 16-bit value toward its target by a step from the structure, adding or subtracting depending on a direction byte, and clamps it at the target, clearing the target once reached. It then looks up the table entry for the new value, stores it in the output field and returns the table index.

name: compute_modulated_offset_step
description: Derives a step value from a phase byte in the structure, using either a table lookup or a ramp index depending on a mode field, multiplies it by a gain nibble, and adds the result to a base word in the structure. It writes the sum to the output and advances the phase byte by a rate nibble.

name: dispatch_channel_command_nibble
description: Decodes a command nibble from a channel structure and dispatches it through a sixteen-way switch that updates volume, slide, period and sequence fields. Several cases are gated on a port register value, and the result is stored in the output field and returned as a status value.

name: store_low_nibble_field
description: Stores the low four bits of a byte from the caller's structure into a second byte field of the same structure. It has no other effect.

name: stub_return_only
description: Entry whose decompiled body is only a return, with no calls, memory access or register use. Its listing has 35 instructions, but the pseudo-code shows no effect, so it has no observable behaviour in the evidence.

name: integer_sqrt_approximation
description: Computes an integer square root of an unsigned input by starting from a bit-length estimate and repeating divide-and-average steps until the estimate stops changing. The final estimate is left only in registers and is not stored to memory.

name: set_status_bits_by_index
description: Sets fixed status bits three and five in the byte at the address register, and sets one bit in a status byte of the structure, with the bit position taken from the low three bits of the data register.

name: patch_jump_stubs_then_call
description: Writes jump-instruction stubs with absolute targets into fixed offsets of a structure, sets a global to zero, and then calls a function pointer stored in the structure. The pseudo-code also shows a call through the incoming pointer's dispatch slot.

description: Checks a 32-bit word in the code area against a fixed value; depending on the result it writes jump-instruction stubs with absolute targets into several code locations, or into other locations. name: call_one_unnamed_routine

name: patch_jump_stubs_and_dispatch

name: write_jump_stubs_then_call
description: Writes jump-instruction stubs with absolute targets into fixed offsets of the structure, then calls through an indirect pointer stored in the structure.

name: decode_keyboard_serial_byte

name: call_hook_then_optional_handler

name: call_offset_handler_return_one

name: call_hook_then_optional_handler
description: Calls the function pointer at offset thirty-six in a global table and, if it returns non-zero, calls a second function pointer at offset eight in the same table.

name: call_offset_handler_return_one
description: Calls the function pointer at offset twelve in a global table and then returns one in the high register pair.

name: call_routine_then_hook
description: Calls a routine, then calls the function pointer at offset forty in a global table, and returns the first routine's result.

name: classify_magic_word_value
description: Compares a 32-bit value in a data register against two fixed constants and stores a code of two or three in a global when one matches, with one as the default. It returns without any other effect.

name: call_global_hook_slot
description: Calls the function pointer at a fixed offset in a global table, passing the data registers through unchanged, and returns them.

name: call_hook_return_saved_value
description: Calls the function pointer at offset forty in a global table, then returns the value that was on the stack on entry.

name: store_then_call_three_routines

name: load_hunk_header_entries
description: When the first longword equals the AmigaDOS hunk header code, it skips the name list, reads a count and fills a stack table from the following entries, calling a routine for each one. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: stub_return_one
description: Returns the constant one with no other effect; the listing has a single instruction.

name: copy_words_then_zero_fill
description: Copies a counted block of longwords from the source pointer into the destination taken from the caller's structure, then zero-fills the remaining bytes up to the size stored there, and returns one.

name: copy_words_then_zero_fill
description: Copies a counted block of longwords from the source pointer into the destination taken from the caller's structure, then zero-fills the remaining bytes up to the size stored there, and returns one.

name: accumulate_table_into_pointers
description: Walks a table of records whose first word is a count, adding a value from the stack frame into each target location addressed through the caller's structure. It stops at a zero count and returns one.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns the constant zero with no other effect; the listing has a single instruction.

name: stub_return_only
description: Routine consisting only of a return, with no calls, memory access or register use; the listing has a single instruction.

name: stub_return_one

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns the constant zero with no other effect; the listing has sixteen instructions and no calls.

name: zero_fill_longword_block
description: Writes zero to each longword of a block whose count comes from the first input and whose address comes from the caller's structure, then returns one.

name: decompress_tagged_bitstream_block
description: Checks a four-character signature at the start of the input and, if it matches, unpacks the data from a bit stream. Each step either copies bytes from the input into the output, writing from the end backwards, or copies earlier output, with run lengths and distances read through lookup tables.

name: transfer_disk_sectors_by_track
description: Converts a byte offset into a track and sector position by dividing by twelve sectors per track, then transfers the requested byte count through repeated calls, advancing sector by sector until the count is used up. It returns the final status from the last call.

name: poll_disk_ready_clear_entries
description: Polls the port register up to three times for a flag bit; when it sets, it zeroes two words in each of twelve per-unit table entries and returns the result of a called routine. If the flag never sets, it returns the failure code twenty-nine.

name: setup_disk_dma_read_buffer
description: Writes control and sync values to the disk controller registers and stores the incoming buffer address in the disk pointer register, then sets the transfer length before returning.

name: decode_mfm_sector_headers
description: Reads sector headers from a raw track buffer, checks each one against a fixed sync word and a checksum, and decodes the odd and even bit streams of the sector fields. It returns zero after twelve sectors, or error code twenty-five or twenty-seven when a header does not match.

name: wait_for_table_word_nonzero
description: Calls a routine and then calls another in a loop that returns once a table word in the caller's structure becomes non-zero, or after the second call. It returns zero or the result of the second routine.

name: fold_xor_checksum_block
description: XORs 256 longwords together and keeps only the alternating bits, then folds the high half of that value into the low half to form the returned checksum.

name: interleave_bits_xor_chain
description: Interleaves two bit-planes stored 128 longwords apart, as in the bit-merge routine, and XORs each merged longword with the previous one before writing it to the output.

name: halve_table_entry_store
description: Halves a 16-bit entry in a global table, selected by a field of the caller's structure, after calling a routine to obtain a pointer if the entry is negative. It then stores the incoming word through that pointer and records the result of another routine in a global.

name: poll_port_clear_table_entry
description: Polls a global flag for up to 86 iterations, calling a routine between polls. When bit four clears, it zeroes a table entry chosen by the caller's structure and stores the result of another routine in a global; if the flag never clears, it returns without a value.

name: build_port_mask_clear_bit
description: Builds a port control byte from the data byte by clearing one bit, chosen by an index in the caller's structure, and clears bit two when a table flag for that index is set. The result is returned in the data register.

name: pulse_port_bits_count
description: Repeats a count taken from the data register: each pass calls a routine, clears bit one of the result when a second value is non-negative, sets bit zero in the port register, and calls another routine.

name: write_adkcon_conditional_bit
description: Writes a fixed control value to ADKCON and, when a signed value in the caller's frame is negative, writes a byte built from a computed bit index to the same register.

name: set_bit_in_global_flag
description: Sets one bit in the data byte passed in, with the bit position taken from an index in the caller's frame offset by three and masked to five bits. It writes the result to the CIA port register.

name: reset_ciab_port_then_wait
description: Writes all ones to the CIA port register, calls a called routine once, then repeatedly calls it again and waits while the low bit of the port register stays set, until the call returns one. Returns zero.

name: wait_for_flag_and_result
description: Calls a routine and, while the low bit of the port register stays set, waits; it repeats until the call returns one, then returns zero.

name: configure_cia_timer_if_idle
description: When the low bit of the port register is clear and a value from the caller's frame is not one, it writes three fixed control values to the CIA timer register in order.

name: set_ciab_timer
description: Writes three fixed values in sequence to the CIA B timer control, timer high-byte and timer low-byte registers.

name: stub_return_stack_value
description: Returns the value that was on the stack at entry, with no other effect; the listing has two instructions and no calls.

name: stub_return_stack_value
description: Returns the value that was on the stack at entry, with no other effect; the listing has two instructions and no calls.

name: stub_single_instruction_unidentified
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the listed facts are known: a single instruction that the reference run executed, reached from outside the normal flow. No purpose can be drawn from it.

name: configure_copper_and_interrupts
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the listed facts are known: it writes to the copper list pointer and the interrupt enable register, makes eight calls to unnamed routines, and runs 63 instructions. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: poll_port_bit_bounded
description: Waits up to 200 passes, calling wait_for_raster_line between checks, while bit seven of a global is set. When the bit clears it sets the global to one and returns the remaining count; if the bit never clears it returns zero.

name: call_four_unnamed_routines
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code, so only the listed facts are known: thirteen instructions that make calls to four unnamed routines, and it is called by the tiny return routine.

name: fill_copper_list_entries
description: Fills a counted table of eight-byte records: each record receives the low and high words of a 32-bit value that increases by a fixed step per record. The copper list pointer and beam-position registers are also touched by the surrounding facts.

name: copy_sixteen_longwords_block
description: Copies sixteen longwords from one fixed memory address to another, one longword per pass.

name: wait_for_raster_result_one
description: Repeatedly calls wait_for_raster_line until the value it returns is one, then returns zero.

name: store_value_and_delay
description: Calls a routine and, if it returns non-zero, stores that value in a global, runs a delay loop of forty thousand passes that writes the low word to the same global each pass, and returns the value. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: delay_loop_write_global
description: Runs a loop of forty thousand passes, writing the low word of its counter to a global each pass, and returns the incoming data register unchanged.

name: fill_bitplane_pointer_records
description: Writes a control value, then fills six eight-byte records with the low and high words of a 32-bit pointer that advances by a fixed step per record. The DMA control register is also touched by the surrounding facts.

name: zero_block_between_calls
description: Calls one routine, zeroes 2560 longwords starting at a fixed address, then calls a second routine.

name: wait_raster_until_global_set
description: Calls one routine, then repeatedly calls two routines, including wait_for_raster_line, until a global becomes non-zero.

name: wait_raster_until_global_set
description: Calls one routine, then repeatedly calls two routines, including wait_for_raster_line, until a global becomes non-zero.

name: wait_struct_word_nonzero
description: Spins until the word at offset six in the caller's structure becomes non-zero, then returns, with no other effect.

name: convert_colour_words_to_channels
description: Sets the state word to two, clears a block of 48 longwords, then converts a counted list of 16-bit colour words into three channel values per word, each four-bit channel divided by fifteen. The interrupt enable register is also touched according to the facts.

name: step_channels_toward_target
description: When a state word equals two and a counter has reached its limit, it walks a table of three-nibble colour entries and adds a per-channel delta wherever a channel differs from its target. When no channel changes, it sets a completion flag and clears the state word.

name: step_struct_channels_toward_target
description: Uses the state and table pointers stored in the caller's structure to walk the three-nibble colour entries, adding a per-channel delta wherever a channel differs from its target. When nothing changes it marks the structure done and clears its state word.

name: init_colour_channel_tables
description: Sets the state word to three, clears a block of 48 longwords, then fills one table with channel values divided by fifteen and a second table with the raw four-bit channels from a counted list of 16-bit colour words. It also clears a global.

name: step_channels_down_toward_target
description: When the state word equals three and a counter has reached its limit, it walks a table of three-nibble colour entries and subtracts a per-channel delta from each channel that is still non-zero. When no channel is non-zero it sets a completion flag and clears the state word.

name: step_struct_channels_down
description: Uses the state and table pointers stored in the caller's structure to walk the three-nibble colour entries, subtracting a per-channel delta from each channel that is still non-zero. When none remain it marks the structure done and clears its state word.

name: parse_iff_ilbm_palette
description: Checks the form and image-type signatures of an IFF ILBM file, walks its chunks to find the bitmap header, body and colour map, and packs the three-byte colour triples of the colour map into 12-bit colour words written to the output array.

name: unpack_run_length_signed_bytes
description: Expands the same run-length byte format as its neighbour but returns nothing and keeps its count in a signed byte, looping while the count is non-negative.

name: set_global_call_then_return
description: Clears a global, stores a 16-bit argument in another global, calls a fixed routine, then calls a second routine and returns its result. It spins forever instead when a flag is set.

name: poll_code_and_dispatch
description: When a global is zero, calls a fixed routine and checks the returned byte. A code of minus one hundred and nineteen makes it call another routine and return, and a code of minus one hundred and eighteen sets a global to 255.

name: run_pause_screen_loop
description: Saves several globals, sets two timing values, and loops calling a routine until it returns a code, then restores the globals and returns that code, or zero when it is minus one hundred and nineteen. The text PAUSED is referenced.

name: build_bit_reversed_table
description: Fills a 256-byte table with the bit-reversed value of each index, starting from the address held in a global.

name: relocate_record_tree
description: Walks a block of fixed-size records addressed by offsets from the input header, adds the base address to pointer fields, and shifts an extent field right by four bits. It copies the records into an output list and calls a routine for each entry.

name: expand_bitmask_table_pairs
description: Walks a 16-bit mask from its low bit, and for each set bit copies table-indexed byte pairs from the source into interleaved output columns, moving through the source with a row stride.

name: skip_until_negative_byte
description: Advances through a byte stream, calling a routine for each byte, while the current byte is non-negative. It returns the first negative byte it reaches.

name: decode_control_byte_stream
description: Copies a sixteen-entry header into an output table, doubling each value, then processes a counted stream of control bytes. Negative values, zero and one select different copy or repeat actions, and other values copy words through a called routine into the output.

name: clamp_offset_to_window
description: Wraps an offset that lies outside a 38-unit window by a fixed step, and returns the first argument when the result equals a comparison value. Otherwise it returns the data registers unchanged.

name: spin_forever_stub
description: Routine that does nothing but loop forever. The decompiler removed unreachable blocks around it, and the listing shows no visible work.

name: call_routine_per_text_char
description: Walks a null-terminated text, calling a routine for each character, then returns zero.

name: draw_glyph_into_bitplanes
description: Maps a character to a six-bit glyph index, skipping spaces. For sixteen rows it combines pairs of glyph bytes into four bitplanes spaced 8000 bytes apart, using AND and OR operations to draw one glyph.

name: call_routine_per_text_char
description: Walks a null-terminated text, calling a routine for each character, then returns zero.

name: draw_glyph_into_bitplanes_narrow
description: Maps a character to a glyph index, skipping NUL and space characters. It then combines eight rows of glyph byte pairs into four bitplanes spaced 8000 bytes apart, using AND and OR operations.

name: stub_return_stack_value
description: Returns the value that was on the stack at entry, with no other effect; the listing has three instructions and no calls.

name: call_routine_per_text_char
description: Walks a null-terminated text, calling a routine for each character, then returns zero.

name: draw_glyph_bitplane_masks
description: Maps a character to a glyph index, skipping spaces. For sixteen rows it applies AND masks to bitplanes spaced 8000 bytes apart and ORs one byte into a third plane, drawing one glyph.

name: reset_global_state_words
description: Clears several global state words, calls a routine four times, then clears one more global state word and returns the incoming data register.

name: init_channel_record_fields
description: Writes zero to a word in each of two structures, and sets one word of the first structure to one and another to zero.

name: dispatch_table_entries_for_index
description: Converts its argument to a zero-based index. Outside the range zero to twenty-three it calls a routine; inside that range it calls a routine for each non-zero entry of a four-word row in a fixed table, and returns the argument unchanged.

name: call_nonzero_table_row_entries
description: Walks a four-word row of a fixed table chosen by the argument, calling a routine for each non-zero entry, then returns the stacked value.

name: scan_words_skipping_zeros
description: Calls a routine, then scans a counted word array, skipping zero entries. Each time it finds a non-zero word it calls the routine again, and it returns when the count runs out.

name: parse_channel_script_commands
description: Initialises up to four channel records from a table of script pointers, clearing each channel's state and reading control bytes: a non-negative byte selects a table entry, while specific negative codes set pointer and byte fields. A flag bit in a global is set when the scan finishes.

name: update_channel_flag_words
description: Checks a global flag and, when it is set, calls a routine for each of four stored words that is non-zero, merging their bits into a status word. It then keeps only the top two bits of that status word.

name: advance_channel_sequence_tick
description: Decrements a countdown in a channel record and, when it reaches zero, reloads the record's sequence pointer and dispatches the next command byte. The decompiled output is dominated by bad instruction data and a long case switch, so only this outline is reliable.

name: update_channel_period_and_volume
description: Recomputes a channel's period from a table indexed by the record's note, applying a slide step and a volume value when the matching flag bits are set, and stores the results in the channel record. Parts of the decompiled output are bad instruction data, so only this outline is reliable.

name: tail_call_unnamed_routine
description: Two-instruction entry that makes one call to an unnamed routine; the decompiled body is bad instruction data, so no further behaviour is supported.

name: call_unnamed_routine_once
description: Three-instruction entry that calls one unnamed routine; the decompiled body is bad instruction data, so no further behaviour is supported.

name: tail_call_unnamed_routine
description: Two-instruction entry that makes one call to an unnamed routine; the decompiled body is bad instruction data, so no further behaviour is supported.

name: tail_call_unnamed_routine

name: advance_channel_stream_pointer
description: Reads one byte from a channel's sequence stream, adds it to a 16-bit field in the channel record, and stores the advanced stream pointer back in the record. Parts of the listing are bad instruction data, so only this outline is reliable.

name: call_unnamed_routine_once
description: Four-instruction entry that calls one unnamed routine; the decompiled body is bad instruction data, so no further behaviour is supported.

name: update_channel_table_word
description: Computes an index from a channel field and a table value, stores a word into a channel table, and calls one unnamed routine. Parts of the decompiled output are bad instruction data, so only this outline is reliable.

name: run_channel_sequence_commands
description: Processes the sequence commands of one channel: it loads a note table entry from a byte in the stream, sets the channel's period and volume fields, updates status bits, and advances the stream pointer. The decompiled listing is partly bad instruction data, so only this outline is reliable.

name: flush_pending_channel_flags
description: When a pending flag word is non-zero, copies table words into the channel record, then sets bit fifteen of a status word from the pending word and clears the pending word. It calls a small merge routine as well.

name: copy_boot_words_block
description: Stores the argument in two record fields, sets a status word, calls a routine, then copies a block of 500 words from a fixed source to a fixed destination and calls another routine. The listing ends in bad instruction data, so its tail is not reliable.

name: copy_words_block_500
description: Writes a fixed byte pattern at offsets relative to two base pointers, copies four words and then 500 words from fixed source addresses to fixed destinations, and calls a routine. The listing ends in bad instruction data, so its tail is not reliable.

name: copy_words_block_500
description: Copies a block of 500 words from one fixed address to another, then calls a routine. The listing then reaches bad instruction data, so the tail is not reliable.

name: store_handler_pointer_field
description: Stores the address of a routine into offset eight of a structure passed in the address register, then returns.

name: install_handlers_and_jump
description: Copies a table of words from a fixed source into the low code area, calls two routines, and calls a handler through a pointer. It runs optional follow-up calls when two flags are non-zero, then jumps to a fixed low address.

name: return_fixed_magic_value
description: Returns a fixed 32-bit magic constant with no other effect; the listing has two instructions and no calls.

name: xor_global_then_call_hook
description: XORs a global with a fixed key in four steps, sets it to 255, then calls a function pointer at offset thirty-two in a structure. It returns the two data registers unchanged.

name: call_routine_pass_through
